{{Quote|But my goals were modest. I neither quested for the ''Queen of Ranroon'' nor sought to test my theory about the coordinates of lost Astigone. I was after something much less consequential, and yet more surprising in its absence.|Bleys Harand, ''Travels Amid Strange Stars''|<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-3-xim-the-despot|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 3 - "Xim the Despot"}}</ref>}}
'''OHS3842-03''', at one point known as '''Astigone''', was an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Ash Worlds/Legends|Ash Worlds]] [[Sector/Legends|sector]]. Around [[25,100 BBY]], Astigone was designated as the [[Xim Thrones|Eighth Throne]] of the [[Xim's empire|empire]] of the [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] conqueror [[Xim/Legends|Xim]]. Over the subsequent [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]], the knowledge of Astigone's location became lost and was subject to much [[Scholar/Legends|scholarly]] debate. The [[Xenoarchaeology/Legends|xenoarchaeologist]] [[Henrietya Antilles]] ultimately re-discovered Astigone's identity with the help of a [[Antilles Map|document]] found in the [[Great Duinarbulon Mausoleum]].

==Description==
OHS3842-03 was the alphanumerical designation of a lush [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Xim Week">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-the-history-of-xim-and-the-tion-cluster|text=Essential Atlas Extra: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}}</ref> located in the [[OHS3842-03 system/Legends|OHS3842-03 system]], a part of the [[Ash Worlds/Legends|Ash Worlds]] [[Sector/Legends|sector]]<ref name="EAOC" /> in [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] of<ref name="TEA Astigone" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC" /> Between [[25,120 BBY]] and [[25,096 BBY]], it was linked by [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] to the [[OHS4140-02 system/Legends|Balshebr]], [[Altratonne system/Legends|Kveror]], and [[Agon system/Legends|Turallun systems]].<ref name="TEA Astigone" />

==History==
[[File:XimsEmpire-TheHistoryOfXimAndTheTionCluster.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Astigone was the Eighth Throne of Xim's empire.]]
By approximately [[25,100 BBY]],<ref name="Xim Week" /> the [[Xim's empire|empire]] of the [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] conqueror [[Xim/Legends|Xim]] [[Xim's Expansionist Period|expanded]] into the region the Tionese named the Kiirium Reaches. That area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] included OHS3842-03,<ref name="TEA Astigone" /> which was then known as Astigone and designated as the Eighth of the [[Xim Thrones]]&mdash;the [[Politics/Legends|politically]] and ceremonially central worlds of his empire. Astigone's location was eventually recorded in a [[Antilles Map|document]] that came to reside in the [[Great Duinarbulon Mausoleum]] on the world [[Duinarbulon]]. Nevertheless, [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] before the [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the precise knowledge of what location Astigone's name&mdash;and even that of the Kiirium Reaches&mdash;referred to had been lost. [[Scholar/Legends|Scholars]] extensively debated the matter, and eventually, many luxury resorts on<ref name="Xim Week" /> the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> world [[Centares/Legends|Centares]] became named after Astigone.<ref name="Xim Week" />

The [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]], [[Philosopher/Legends|philosopher]], and [[Historian/Legends|historian]]<ref name="Xim Week" /> [[Bleys Harand]] at one point [[Author/Legends|authored]] a travelogue, ''[[Travels Amid Strange Stars]]'', concerning<ref name="Author's Cut" /> his<ref name="Xim Week" /> visit to the worlds of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]. In it, Harand noted that the purpose of his voyage&mdash;to discover a contemporary visual depiction of Xim&mdash;was "less consequential" than testing a theory concerning the coordinates of Astigone.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> Eventually, Harand's student [[Henrietya Antilles]],<ref name="Xim Week" /> a [[Xenoarchaeology/Legends|xenoarchaeologist]]<ref name="TEA" /> active during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="Journal8">{{JournalCite|8|The Gree Enclave}}</ref> re-discovered the Great Duinarbulon Mausoleum, and Astigone's identity became known once again due to the information in the document—named the "Antilles Map"—stored therein.<ref name="Xim Week" />

==Behind the scenes==
OHS3842-03 was introduced via a label on a map by [[Modi]] included in<ref name="TEA Astigone" /> the [[August 18]], [[2009]]<ref name="Penguin">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/185066/the-essential-atlas-star-wars-by-daniel-wallace-and-jason-fry|text=The Essential Atlas: Star Wars}}</ref> reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', which was authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]]. The book placed OHS3842-03 in grid square T-7.<ref name="TEA Astigone" /> OHS3842-03, or Astigone, was first described as a planet by the [[December 7]], 2009 [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]]<ref name="XimOriginal">{{SWArchive|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek01/index.html|text=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}}</ref> article "[[Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster]]" by Fry. In one instance, a map included with the article misidentified the planet as the Seventh Throne of Xim's empire.<ref name="Xim Week" />

OHS3842-03 was originally meant to be mentioned in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by Fry and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]; however, the section that would have mentioned it was cut before the book's release. The information regarding the planet was later released in [[2013]] as part of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], a series of articles published on the StarWars.com [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] by Fry and<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[Del Rey]] editor<ref name="Celestials">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut — The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] containing various cut content from ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.<ref name="Author's Cut" />
